plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy since you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid. Overbidding risks winning at a price above my value (negative profit), while underbidding risks losing profitable opportunities where I'd win at a price below my value. With no prior history to suggest otherwise, truthful bidding maximizes expected profit regardless of competitors' strategies. My value is $35, so I will bid exactly that amount.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of what other bidders do. This is because you pay the second-highest bid if you win, not your own bid, so bidding higher than value risks overpaying, and bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. With a value of $32, the optimal strategy is to bid exactly $32, ensuring I win whenever it's profitable and pay a fair price only if I do win.

In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid, not your own bid, so overbidding risks losses on ties/overpayment and underbidding risks losing profitable auctions. With my value at $48, I should bid exactly $48 to guarantee optimal outcomes - winning whenever profitable and never overpaying.
